A.title: Lightweight In-Browser LLMs for JSON to Chart.js Config Conversion?
A.body:
I'm looking into running small language models entirely in the browser to convert JSON data into valid Chart.js configurations. The goal is to keep everything lightweight and client-side, but the hardware and browser environments of users are unknown, which complicates tool selection.

Has anyone found effective in-browser inference frameworks that handle this kind of structured generation well without heavy dependencies? Given the variability in users' setups, I'm curious about practical tradeoffs or recommendations for frameworks that balance model size, speed, and reliability in-browser.

Any experiences or pointers to lightweight tools that can specifically assist with JSON-to-Chart.js config generation would be really helpful.

B.title: Seeking Recommendations for Lightweight In-Browser LLMs to Convert JSON into Chart.js Configs
B.body: I'm exploring the feasibility of running small language models entirely within a web browser, aiming to transform JSON data into valid Chart.js configurations for visualization. Additionally, generating brief natural language summaries of the data is a secondary goal. Key requirements include support for small quantized models ideally under 100MB, and runtimes compatible with WebGPU or WASM for efficient client-side inference. I've started looking into MLC.ai as a promising option but haven't found detailed community feedback on its effectiveness for this specific task. Has anyone here experimented with in-browser LLM inference frameworks for structured data transformation or visualization generation? If so, what models and prompting approaches worked best? Also curious about alternative runtimes or tools that might better support these use cases, especially those optimized for lightweight, browser-native deployments.
